models_evaluated: reinforcement learning model with expert-derived reward table

links.outcome: Model performance when decision criteria weigh benefits and harms of diagnostic errors versus naive supervised learning
links.effect: Reward-adjusted RL and threshold-based models outperformed naive supervised learning in various clinical scenarios; RL raised melanoma sensitivity from 61.4% to 79.5% and basal cell carcinoma sensitivity from 79.4% to 87.1%.
links.quote: We further demonstrated that the reward-adjusted reinforcement learning model and a threshold-based model outperformed naïve supervised learning in various clinical scenarios.

unlisted_practices: Incorporating expert-generated nonuniform reward and penalty tables into AI training via reinforcement learning to reflect human preferences about diagnostic error harms

screen.reason: The study tests the impact of incorporating expert clinical utility tables (balancing harms and benefits of errors via reinforcement learning rewards/thresholds) into AI decision support on dermatologist diagnostic accuracy and management decisions.
